summary: Jackson County, OR lookout on Bessie Rock: built 1931, staffed 1941 and 1953, removed or destroyed in 1969; no source describes the summit today.

facts.design: Enclosed 6-foot base with an L-4 cab, reached by ladders (an 85-foot ladder in a 1932 article; 96 rungs in a 1941 account)
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1969; the sources differ on which

staffing.status: Staffed 105 days in 1941 (Roy G. Pursel); fire spotter in 1953

visit.trail_note: Lookout gone; no source describes the summit today or a current route to it. A 2015 review says the old telephone line and much of the trail were abandoned in the 1960s.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Rogue River National Forest

events.note: Register and firelookout date it to 1931; the Medford Mail Tribune reported work on the station in October 1931; a January 1932 article describes it as a new station
Staffed 105 days; Roy G. Pursel was the lookout that summer; communications via Columbia Utilities Company to the Butte Falls Ranger Station
A 17-year-old fire spotter at the lookout had an emergency appendectomy and was carried down 3.5 miles of trail
Register says removed; firelookout and Forest Lookouts say destroyed
Registered November 22, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1969; firelookout and Forest Lookouts say destroyed in 1969. The record keeps the lookout as gone with a 1969 event and does not choose between the two words.
The register and firelookout give 5,953 ft (1,814 m). The 1933 NGS datasheet quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 5959 ft. The record keeps the register figure, 1814.5 m as in the brief.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 25.9 looks like the 85-foot ladder, so it was removed from the story in the 2026-10-09 fact-check. Brief kind 'ground' may not fit: sources describe an enclosed base with a cab reached by ladder on a rock; left unchanged for a human to decide. A search result for a Forest Service photo record (picryl.com, not opened, returned 403) gives the build date as ca. 1934, which conflicts with the 1931 date; unverified and not used in the story. Source [4] is a user review on a trip-listing site and is hedged in the story. No access level set: no source describes public access today. No photos added. Checker (height_m): our record's 25.9 m may be wrong: 25.9 m matches the 85-foot ladder the 1932 article describes, not the height of the structure. No source read gives an overall height.
